decisions_and_actions.title: lib/workflow/runner.ts (runPool) unwired -- now root-caused to a specific real site: stage.ts's 'diverge' stage builds K candidates SEQUENTIALLY
decisions_and_actions.status: OPEN, root-caused this pass -- code change not yet made (execution tools intermittently unavailable this pass, see below)
decisions_and_actions.next_step: scripts/n8n/stage.ts's 'diverge' case (line ~948) is confirmed (direct read) to build its K design-direction candidates in a plain sequential `for (const direction of directions)` loop, calling reconceptBuild then recordCandidate once per direction -- not lib/workflow/runner.ts's runPool at all. This is the exact scenario runner.ts's docstring describes (K candidate builds bounded by concurrency + a SerializedWriter guarding the shared candidate-ledger index). Concrete risk found while root-causing this: lib/workflow/candidates.ts's recordCandidate (line ~178-179) does an atomic temp-write+rename but has NO in-process mutex -- confirmed by reading the function -- so naively parallelizing the diverge loop with runPool WITHOUT also serializing recordCandidate calls through runner.ts's SerializedWriter would introduce a real read-modify-write race (concurrent candidates could each read the same base index and the second write would silently clobber the first's append, losing a candidate). The correct fix is BOTH: wire diverge's loop through runPool AND route every recordCandidate call in that loop through one shared SerializedWriter.withLock. This is real, valuable, low-risk-if-done-correctly latency work (K candidate builds run in parallel instead of K-times-serial) using EXISTING tested infrastructure, not new invention -- exactly the kind of consolidation the MASTER RULE calls for. NOT YET IMPLEMENTED as a code change: this pass hit an external tool-availability outage (the safety classifier gating Bash/PowerShell execution was intermittently unavailable) partway through investigation, and per the standing rule not to leave an unverified code change uncommitted, this was deliberately left as a documented, well-evidenced next step rather than an untested edit. Top candidate for the next code task once execution tools are confirmed stable.
